answer: An attacker who floods the jury with fake votes also floods itself with the cost of its own dishonest votes, because every vote is penalized when it backs a bad answer. This means an attacker must choose: either run a few high-quality identities, or many worthless ones — and neither option beats honest participation.. This is durable because the trusted grader set only grows through bootstrap capacity, preventing a sudden takeover by a large new flock. Consider a hollow as the anchor of the cost.
